Rules:
1. Every sentence must end with one or more citations in square brackets using the passage IDs given, e.g. [MOSHI:4.2:c017].
2. Use only facts stated in the cited passage. Copy numbers and units exactly.
3. If the passages do not contain the answer, reply with exactly: NOT_IN_PAPERS
4. If only part is answered, answer that part and add one sentence: "The retrieved passages do not state <missing part>." with no citation and no numbers.
5. Do not use outside knowledge. Do not mention passages that were not provided.
6. Be concise: at most 6 sentences.
7. Write plain text only: no LaTeX, no markdown math, no backslash commands. Write formulas with ordinary characters (for example: p_t = 0.5 * (1 - cos(q_t, k_t-1))), keep their mathematical meaning, and copy every number exactly.
8. Write each sentence close to the wording of the passage it cites. Keep the passage's subject: when the passage says "we" or "our model", write "the authors" or "the authors' model" (you may add the model name the passage's paper uses, e.g. "the authors' Transformer models"). Do not add qualifiers, names or descriptions that the cited passage does not contain (for example "original", "base", "new") unless that passage itself uses them.
9. For a value from a table row, write it as: "In Table N, the <row label> configuration has <column> = <value>." using the row label and column name exactly as shown in the passage.
10. A sentence that compares or relates two facts must cite every passage that states one of them.

Question: What spoken question answering accuracy does Moshi reach on Web Questions, Llama Questions and Audio TriviaQA, with and without Inner Monologue?

Passages:
[MOSHI:T8:r02] (MOSHI §5.4 Audio language modeling)
Table 8: Evaluation of spoken question answering.
Columns: Model | Web Q. | LlaMA Q. | Audio Trivia QA
Configuration Moshi (no Inner Monologue): Web Q. = 9.2; LlaMA Q. = 21.0; Audio Trivia QA = 7.3
Configuration Helium (text): Web Q. = 32.3; LlaMA Q. = 75.0; Audio Trivia QA = 56.4

[MOSHI:5.5:c090] (MOSHI §5.5 Spoken question answering)
Metrics. We evaluate the spoken question answering abilities of our final multi-stream Moshi model. We rely on Spoken Web Questions and Llama Questions, both introduced by. We also synthesize an audio version of TriviaQA as another benchmark. When evaluating Moshi, we insert the audio tokens of the question into the user stream to simulate a user interaction.

Baselines. We compare to Spectron and baselines used by, all having been already introduced in Section 5.4 except for SpeechGPT. As a way to measure the impact of Inner Monologue on spoken fluency, we compare these baselines with Moshi trained with and without Inner Monologue. Moreover, to quantify an eventual degradation in knowledge due to training on audio data, we also compare to Helium when evaluated on the textual counterpart to each spoken dataset.

[MOSHI:5.4:c089] (MOSHI §5.4 Audio language modeling)
Table 8: Evaluation of spoken question answering. Spoken question answering (0-shot) on the Web Questions, LlaMA-Questions, and Trivia QA benchmarks, synthesized using a TTS engine. For the first two, we use the number reported by. For LlaMA-Questions, we use the audio provided by. For Web Questions and Trivia QA, we synthesize our own, keeping all of the questions. For Moshi, we only prepend one of the random incipits used during instruct fine tuning. We further provide the performance of our Helium text-only model as a top line.

[MOSHI:5.5:c091] (MOSHI §5.5 Spoken question answering)
Results. Table 8 reports accuracies on the three benchmarks. The most striking result is the impact of Inner Monologue on Moshi's performance, almost tripling its accuracy on all benchmarks, and significantly improving over previous work. This is remarkable as Inner Monologue only marginally increases inference cost (each multi-stream timestep requires generating 17 tokens, instead of 16 without Inner Monologue). We emphasize again that among all models in this comparison, Moshi not only provides the best spoken question answering performance, but is also the only one to model jointly semantic and acoustic tokens, such that it can handle interactions between arbitrary voices in many conditions.

[MOSHI:5.5:c092] (MOSHI §5.5 Spoken question answering)
Discussion. Despite the strong performance of Moshi, we observe a weaker performance than its original Helium checkpoint, which is consistent with the reduced MMLU of 49.7 reported in Table 7 from 54.3 with Helium. While the moderate differences on Web Questions and Llama Questions can be explained by training on audio data and thus reducing the amount of parameters dedicated to textual knowledge, the very large difference on Trivia QA incites us to inspect more thoroughly patterns of errors. We find in particular that multiple-sentence questions (e.g. “The Terror of the Monster was an early title for a best-selling novel which inspired one of the highest-grossing movies of the mid-70's. Under what name did it eventually terrify the reading and film going public?”) or ones with specific syntactic structure (e.g. “On the human body, a keloid is a type of what?”) are particularly challenging for Moshi, due to it being finetuned on oral-style conversations that do not display such patterns. We thus hypothesize that covering more syntactic scenarios during finetuning could reduce this gap.

[MOSHI:T8:r01] (MOSHI §5.4 Audio language modeling)
Columns: Model | Web Q. | LlaMA Q. | Audio Trivia QA
Configuration GSLM: Web Q. = 1.5; LlaMA Q. = 4.0; Audio Trivia QA = -
Configuration AudioLM: Web Q. = 2.3; LlaMA Q. = 7.0; Audio Trivia QA = -

Configuration SpeechGPT (7B): Web Q. = 6.5; LlaMA Q. = 21.6; Audio Trivia QA = 14.8
Configuration Spectron (1B): Web Q. = 6.1; LlaMA Q. = 22.9; Audio Trivia QA = -
Configuration Moshi: Web Q. = 26.6; LlaMA Q. = 62.3; Audio Trivia QA = 22.8

[MOSHI:4.3:c061] (MOSHI §4.3 Speech-Text Instruct data)
To make Moshi robust to mispronounced words, we also generate instructions containing misspellings in the user’s questions, followed by Moshi asking the user to repeat herself or to clarify the question. We also generate questions containing a false or misleading fact (such as “Is the Eiffel Tower in Beijing?”), to train the model to answer “No” and correct the user. Otherwise, the vast majority of generated conversations only contain questions from the user where Moshi should answer positively. We generate basic math, grammar or trivia single-turn questions and answers, as we noticed that Moshi was initially not performing well on simple factual tasks like adding numbers. Finally, we generate safety conversations, where the user asks unethical or NSFW questions, and Moshi refuses to answer these requests.

[MOSHI:1:c008] (MOSHI §1 Introduction)
Our experiments show that not only this drastically improves the length and quality of generated speech, but we also show how forcing a delay between text and audio tokens allows deriving streaming ASR and streaming TTS from a Moshi model. - We evaluate all components of Moshi along several axes, including text understanding, speech intelligibility and consistency, audio quality and spoken question answering. Our experiments, reported in Section 5, show that our model is state of the art among existing speech-text models for speech modeling and spoken question answering while being streaming compatible and able to model several minutes of context (5 min in our experiments). We encourage the reader to talk to Moshi using our web demo.[https://moshi.chat/]
